acceptanceCriteria: 0063 source body exactly matches production 20260909203604 with SHA256 identity.
Cc/Bcc fields and count CHECKs are present on both Office drafts and messages; helper normalizes/deduplicates recipients with limit and role revokes.
Office attachment metadata table maintains exactly-one draft/message anchor, tenant-bound composite FKs, size bounds, RLS and explicit browser grants revoked.
Versioned mutate_v3 and queue_v4 RPCs preserve actor/tenant permission and send idempotency/recipient checks and service-role grants.
Previous 0061/0062 optimistic revision/first-reply singleton remain unchanged and 0063 ordered after 0062.
64 SQL baseline, 100% focused tests/typecheck and postcommit sync/replay/risk gates PASS; actual PostgreSQL and Pro-only capability remain BLOCKED.
invariants: Recipient Cc/Bcc count bounded, normalized and duplicate-eliminated, including collision with To where applicable.
No attachment row crosses instance boundary to another tenant draft or Office message.
Exactly one attachment owner among draft_id or message_id.
Direct browser roles cannot read/write Office attachment metadata.
No actual external storage upload, provider mail, live DB execution or email transmission.
forbiddenStates: A cross-tenant attachment draft or message link is accepted on real DB.
An attachment is orphaned or linked to both a draft and a message.
A browser role directly SELECTs or writes attachment metadata through a new grant.
Cc/Bcc over-limit or invalid address input silently accepted by guarded RPC.
Source-only test marks actual Fresh Install/Provider/Pro DONE.

specialistReviews.finding: SECURITY DEFINER RPC actor binding and storage object access cannot be validated by static migration strings.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep blocked until real Postgres RLS/role/tenant tests, server caller session binding and Storage policy/attachment download gates.

specialistReviews.finding: Attachment cross-tenant composite FK requires ID+instance unique indexes and existing office_drafts/messages tables.
specialistReviews.resolution: Canonical migration supplies indexes before attachment table; assert predecessor 0057/0062 and source body identity.

specialistReviews.finding: Combined canonical recipient envelope and attachment metadata is high risk but one SQL source release unit.
specialistReviews.resolution: One 0063 SQL, manifest and tests, exact F15 risk 5/5; no Preview/CI.

specialistReviews.finding: Existing tenants may not have new attachment bucket/recipient arrays or SMTP sender verification.
specialistReviews.resolution: Do not run occupied target/provider operations; require clean-target rehearsal and storage/provider readiness proof.

challenge.scenario: An external actor supplies Cc/Bcc entries with mixed case, whitespace and duplicate of the To recipient.
challenge.finding: Incorrect normalization can create unintended duplicate recipients and leak private message headers.
challenge.resolution: Preserve canonical private.normalize_office_email_list_v1, dedupe with excluded list and per-field count constraints; demand real provider acceptance.

challenge.scenario: A draft payload contains a recipient array with invalid JSON types or >10 distinct addresses.
challenge.finding: Malformed inputs might bypass recipient envelope checks or overload provider recipient limits.
challenge.resolution: Retain office_jsonb_text_array_v1 conversion guard, address validation and cardinality CHECK on drafts/messages.

challenge.scenario: An attachment row references a draft of another webshop while using a locally valid instance_id.
challenge.finding: A data/API worker could leak a tenant draft attachment across organizations.
challenge.resolution: Require composite foreign key (draft_id,instance_id) to office_drafts(id,instance_id), similarly messages.

challenge.scenario: An attachment row uses both draft_id and message_id or neither.
challenge.finding: Ambiguous attachment ownership can leak drafts into inbound messages or create orphan metadata.
challenge.resolution: Retain exactly-one-anchor CHECK on attachment row.

challenge.scenario: Anonymous or authenticated user SELECTs private attachment metadata directly through Data API.
challenge.finding: File names, SHA and provider attachment IDs could reveal private correspondence.
challenge.resolution: Enable RLS and revoke all table grants from public,anon,authenticated; verify effective privileges on disposable target.

challenge.scenario: A forged service_role caller queues email with another operator p_actor or unrelated instance.
challenge.finding: Definer RPC bypasses row-level security and actor impersonation can send across tenant.
challenge.resolution: Preserve source checks and require real server request-to-actor identity proof before final release.

challenge.scenario: A draft v3 autosave arrives with stale revision after another tab already saved new recipients.
challenge.finding: Cc/Bcc may overwrite latest content if revision protection dropped by new version.
challenge.resolution: Preserve expectedRevision optimistic predicate in admin_mutate_office_draft_v3 and add runtime two-tab race later.

challenge.scenario: A migration author copies 0063 only partially, omitting one RPC GRANT/REVOKE or index.
challenge.finding: Table source checks might PASS while live new mail/attachment API fails or is exposed.
challenge.resolution: Verify byte-identical entire canonical SQL body with SHA256 plus versioned RPC grants and dependent tables in regression.
